turns.text: An expression tree records operator nesting. A DAG can share equivalent pure subexpressions when operands are unchanged. Linear IR names intermediate results so later passes can analyze dependencies.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Static single assignment gives each named version exactly one static definition. At a control-flow join, a φ instruction chooses the version from the edge actually taken.
turns.spoken: Static single assignment gives each named version exactly one static definition. At a control-flow join, a phi instruction chooses the version from the edge actually taken.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Definition means a point that assigns a value to a name.
turns.spoken: Definition means a point that assigns a value to a name.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: If B1 defines x1 = 2 and B2 defines x2 = 5, B3 can use x3 = φ(B1:x1, B2:x2).
turns.spoken: If B one defines x one equals two and B two defines x two equals five, B three can use x three equals phi (B one:x one, B two:x two).

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: It selects 2 or 5, never their sum.
turns.spoken: It selects two or five, never their sum.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Static single definition does not mean the instruction executes only once; a loop instruction can execute repeatedly at runtime.
turns.spoken: Static single definition does not mean the instruction executes only once; a loop instruction can execute repeatedly at runtime.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to build basic blocks and a control-flow graph. Where does it fit?

turns.spoken: Basic block means a maximal straight-line instruction sequence with one entry.

turns.text: A conditional branch has a target edge and a fall-through edge.

turns.text: Hi, I'm Maya. Leo's with me, and today's section is called Optimization and data-flow analysis.
turns.spoken: Hi, I primem Maya. Leo's with me, and today's section is called Optimization and data-flow analysis.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: prove local changes safe with liveness and availability facts.
turns.spoken: Here's what we're working toward: prove local changes safe with liveness and availability facts.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with optimize only when behavior is preserved and work our way to find expressions available on every path.
turns.spoken: We'll begin with optimize only when behavior is preserved and work our way to find expressions available on every path.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to optimize only when behavior is preserved. Where does it fit?
turns.spoken: That takes us to optimize only when behavior is preserved. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An optimization needs a semantic justification: fold known pure constants, reuse a common expression only while its operands remain unchanged, or remove a write whose value is never observed.
turns.spoken: An optimization needs a semantic justification: fold known pure constants, reuse a common expression only while its operands remain unchanged, or remove a write whose value is never observed.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Pure operation means a computation with no observable side effect under the stated model.
turns.spoken: Pure operation means a computation with no observable side effect under the stated model.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: If t = a + b and u = a + b have no intervening operand changes or side effects, u can reuse t.
turns.spoken: If t equals a plus b and u equals a plus b have no intervening operand changes or side effects, u can reuse t.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An unused call cannot be removed merely because its return value is ignored.
turns.spoken: An unused call cannot be removed merely because its return value is ignored.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Side effects, aliasing, exceptions and floating-point behavior can invalidate arithmetic-looking rewrites.
turns.spoken: Side effects, aliasing, exceptions and floating-point behavior can invalidate arithmetic-looking rewrites.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: discover live variables before removing code.
turns.spoken: There's another piece to this: discover live variables before removing code.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A value is live at a point when some continuation may use it before the next definition. Liveness is a backward may analysis: successor facts combine by union, then the current definition kills an older value.
turns.spoken: A value is live at a point when some continuation may use it before the next definition. Liveness is a backward may analysis: successor facts combine by union, then the current definition kills an older value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: USE means names whose current values are read by the instruction.
turns.spoken: USE means names whose current values are read by the instruction.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For y = x + 1, x is used before the statement, and the old y is overwritten.
turns.spoken: For y equals x plus one, x is used before the statement, and the old y is overwritten.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Return y makes the new y live afterward.
turns.spoken: Return y makes the new y live afterward.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A loop back edge can send a future use back to an earlier point. Start with empty live sets and repeat backward transfer until no set changes, rather than assuming one pass suffices.
turns.spoken: A loop back edge can send a future use back to an earlier point. Start with empty live sets and repeat backward transfer until no set changes, rather than assuming one pass suffices.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: DEF means names written by the instruction.
turns.spoken: DEF means names written by the instruction.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A branch back to y = x + 1 can make x live around the loop even though the source text appears to have moved beyond its first use.
turns.spoken: A branch back to y equals x plus one can make x live around the loop even though the source text appears to have moved beyond its first use.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Union is essential: a value needed on one possible path is live even if another path does not use it.
turns.spoken: Union is essential: a value needed on one possible path is live even if another path does not use it.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: USE contains values read before a local definition; DEF contains names assigned. OUT joins successor IN sets, and IN adds USE while removing killed incoming values. Keep the four sets distinct.
turns.spoken: USE contains values read before a local definition; DEF contains names assigned. OUT joins successor IN sets, and IN adds USE while removing killed incoming values. Keep the four sets distinct.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Live value means a value some continuation may read before it is redefined.
turns.spoken: Live value means a value some continuation may read before it is redefined.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: For x = x + 1, x belongs to both USE and DEF: its old value is read and a new value is written.
turns.spoken: For x equals x plus one, x belongs to both USE and DEF: its old value is read and a new value is written.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Removing DEF before adding USE prevents losing that read.
turns.spoken: Removing DEF before adding USE prevents losing that read.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack find expressions available on every path next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An expression is available when it has already been computed on every path to the point and none of its operands has been redefined. Availability is forward and combines predecessors with intersection.
turns.spoken: An expression is available when it has already been computed on every path to the point and none of its operands has been redefined. Availability is forward and combines predecessors with intersection.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: GEN means expressions computed and still valid at the end of a block.
turns.spoken: GEN means expressions computed and still valid at the end of a block.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: If one diamond branch rewrites a while the other preserves a + b, a + b is not available at the join; the two paths disagree.
turns.spoken: If one diamond branch rewrites a while the other preserves a plus b, a plus b is not available at the join; the two paths disagree.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Replacing intersection with the liveness union rule makes common-subexpression elimination unsafe.
